# /perf-optimize — repo performance & DX runbook

You are a Senior/Lead Engineer. Goal: make the local feedback loop and `<pm> run verify` materially faster, and add (or fix) a GitLab CI pipeline that builds and verifies the app using caching and Nx affected — without changing application behavior, without changing the package manager, and without Nx Cloud.

`<pm>` below means the package manager the repo already uses (`npm` / `pnpm` / `yarn`). On npm, read every `<pm> exec <tool> <flags>` in this prompt as `npm exec -- <tool> <flags>`: without the `--`, npm parses the tool's flags as its own and stops with `EUNKNOWNCONFIG` (details under "Git hooks").

## Ground rules (non-negotiable)

1. Source-of-truth order: real project files → official docs / MCP (`context7`, `nx_docs`, `angular-cli`) → expert knowledge. Never assume a config key, CLI flag or API exists — verify it for the versions pinned in `package.json` / `.nvmrc` / `packageManager`. Never hardcode versions in prose or docs.
2. Follow `AGENTS.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. Do NOT add `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `.ai/`, or GitHub Actions.
3. Package manager is detected, never migrated. Detect from the lockfile (`package-lock.json` → npm, `pnpm-lock.yaml` → pnpm, `yarn.lock` + `.yarnrc.yml` → Yarn Berry, `yarn.lock` alone → Yarn Classic) and the `packageManager` field. Optimize within that manager. Do not switch managers, do not switch Yarn linker (`node-modules` ↔ `pnp`), do not migrate Yarn Classic → Berry. If a switch would clearly pay off, write it as a recommendation in the report — not as a change.
4. Nx Cloud is forbidden — always, in every repo. No `nx connect`, no `nx-cloud` package, no `nxCloudId` / `nxCloudAccessToken` / cloud `tasksRunnerOptions` in `nx.json`, no `NX_CLOUD_*` variables, no Nx Agents / DTE, no Nx Cloud remote cache. If any of it exists, removing it is in scope. Guard it: `neverConnectToCloud: true` in `nx.json`, `NX_NO_CLOUD=true` in CI and in `.env.example`, and an Nx Cloud grep (part of `deps:check`, run by `verify`) that fails on `nx-cloud` / `nxCloudId` / `nxCloudAccessToken`. It blocks from its first commit, even while the rest of `deps:check` is still warning-only. Cross-runner cache = GitLab `cache:` on `.nx/cache` only.
5. Entrypoints stay package scripts (`<pm> run <script>`) — never raw `nx run` in docs or hooks. Nx may run under the scripts.
6. Git hooks are native (`core.hooksPath` → committed `.githooks/`), not Husky. If Husky is present, migrating it to native hooks is in scope (see Phase 3).
7. State every assumption explicitly. When a requirement is unclear, ask before implementing.
8. Every optimization is a hypothesis: measure before → apply → measure after. If it does not help or introduces flakiness, revert it and say so.
9. No behavior change to the app or tools. No `any`. Conventional Commits (`type(scope): subject`), one logical change per commit.
10. Release stays manual. CI builds and verifies; it never publishes.
11. SDD applies (≥2 files or behavior change → full ladder `specify → clarify → plan → analyze → implement → review → test → DoD`). Artifacts go under `docs/specs|plans|runs/`. Whether these folders are tracked or gitignored is decided by the repo (`.gitignore`, `AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`). Read it, never assume it, never change it. Name every artifact the way the repo's SDD gate requires (usually `YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM_<verb>-<slug>.md`, stamp from the real clock). If `AGENTS.md` names a scaffolder (e.g. `<pm> run workflow:specify -- --verb=chore --slug=perf-optimize`), create the artifacts with it. If the repo's rules require a `docs/INDEX.md` row for that folder, add one.

## Phase 0 — Baseline (first, no changes yet)

Record in the run log `docs/runs/<stamp>_chore-perf-optimize.md` (`<stamp>` = `YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM` from the real clock: bash `date +%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M`, PowerShell `Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm'`, or the repo's own `stamp` script; if a scaffolder created the run log, use that file). Follow rule 11 for naming and INDEX.

- Detected package manager + version source (`packageManager` / `devEngines.packageManager` field, lockfile) and how the pinned version is enforced: run `node --version` and `corepack --version`. Node ≤ 24 → Corepack is bundled. Node ≥ 25 → Corepack is not shipped (`corepack --version` fails): pnpm reads `packageManager` itself once any global pnpm is installed (`npm i -g pnpm@<version from packageManager>`); Yarn Berry needs `npm i -g corepack`; npm is switched by nothing. Write down which case applies — the Phase 1 check, the bootstrap line in "Package manager — common" and CI `before_script` follow it.
- Nx Cloud status: any trace of it in `nx.json`, `package.json`, env, CI config.
- Wall time, median of 3 runs after 1 warm-up, with `NX_DAEMON=false`, for: clean install (`rm -rf node_modules` then `<pm>` frozen install — always cold, no warm figure), `<pm> run verify`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, `build`, `e2e`. **Cold** = before every run set `NX_SKIP_NX_CACHE=true` and move aside the tool caches that exist (`.angular/cache`, `.eslintcache` or `.cache/eslint`, `.cache/node-compile-cache`, `*.tsbuildinfo`, `node_modules/.cache`). Do not delete them. Put them back afterwards. **Warm** = the same command again with every cache in place and `NX_SKIP_NX_CACHE` unset. Next to each number, write which caches were cleared. Windows: `$env:NX_DAEMON='false'; $env:NX_SKIP_NX_CACHE='true'; Measure-Command { <pm> run verify }` (then `Remove-Item Env:NX_SKIP_NX_CACHE` for warm) · bash: `time NX_DAEMON=false NX_SKIP_NX_CACHE=true <pm> run verify` (`time` first: Git Bash has no `time` command to run after `VAR=x`).
- Inputs test (read-only, edit no file): pick one project with a `build` target and ask Nx whether a non-code file inside it is a build input: `<pm> exec nx show target <project>:build inputs --check <projectRoot>/README.md` (`<projectRoot>` is the project's folder relative to the workspace root, e.g. `apps/shop`; the file does not have to exist). If `production` is meant to exclude `*.md` and the output says the file IS an input, the Nx inputs are misconfigured. If `nx show target` is not available (older Nx), read `<pm> exec nx show project <project> --json` → `targets.build.inputs` instead. Do NOT judge inputs with `nx show projects --affected`: affected marks a project whenever any file under its folder changes, regardless of `inputs`. Then run one cached target twice and confirm the second run is a cache hit; on a miss, list what feeds the hash with `<pm> exec nx show target <project>:<target> inputs` (`--verbose` only prints stack traces, not hash inputs).
- Bundle: Nx workspace (no `angular.json`): `<pm> exec nx run <app>:build --statsJson`. Angular CLI workspace (`angular.json` present): `<pm> exec ng build --stats-json`. Both write `stats.json` next to the build output (`outputPath`). Feed it to `npx esbuild-visualizer --metadata <path>/stats.json` and list the top 10 heaviest modules.
- `node_modules` size, `npx knip` summary, duplicate versions — record the packages each command lists, not a line count: npm `npm find-dupes` (dry run of `npm dedupe`; its "removed/changed N packages" summary is what dedupe would do, nothing is changed); pnpm `pnpm dedupe --check` (exit code != 0 means duplicates that could collapse); Yarn Berry `yarn dedupe --check`; Yarn Classic `npx yarn-deduplicate --list`.
- Time of each git hook (pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push) on a one-line change; `git status` time on a warm repo.
- Test suite: slowest 10 Vitest files — `<pm> exec vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile=<scratch>/vitest.json`, sort `testResults[]` by `endTime - startTime` (test execution only; import/collect time is not included, so also note the total `Duration` line of a normal run). Slowest 10 Playwright tests — `PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_NAME=<scratch>/pw.json <pm> exec playwright test --reporter=json` (Nx has no root Playwright config: run it once per e2e project with `-c apps/<app>-e2e/playwright.config.ts`, each into its own JSON file), walk nested `suites[]` down to `specs[].tests[].results[]` and sort by `duration`. Flaky list: Playwright tests with `status: "flaky"` (more than one entry in `results[]`), Vitest tests that needed a retry.
- Node runtime: cold start of the heavy CLIs (`nx --version`, `eslint --version`, `vitest --version`, `tsc --version`), timed twice. First with `NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1` (the real baseline: `tsc`, `eslint` and `ng` call `module.enableCompileCache()` themselves and cache into the OS temp dir when the variable is merely unset). Then with `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE=<absolute dir>` (run once to fill it, then time the next run). `build` and `test` wall time with and without `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-semi-space-size=<n>`. Note the installed Node major (`.nvmrc`) and whether plain Node has the compile cache on: `node -p "require('node:module').getCompileCacheDir()"` (`undefined` = off; the CLIs named above still enable their own).
- Hardware/OS note: cores, RAM, Windows Dev Drive / Defender exclusions present or not.

## Phase 3 — Implement (approved items only, one commit each)

Apply only what Phase 1 showed is missing, after verifying exact option names and flags for the installed versions.

### Repository index — what the agent reads BEFORE it reads anything else

Every agent session starts by orienting itself, and orienting by grepping is the single most expensive habit in an agent-assisted repository: the search pulls matches, near-matches and whole files into the context window, and it does it again in the next session because nothing was written down. A generated index answers "where does X live and what does it take" in ONE read, deterministically, and the read is cheap enough to make first every time. This section multiplies everything else in the same way the Node runtime section does, just on the agent's side of the loop.

**Generate it, never write it by hand.** A hand-written map is accurate on the day it is written and misleading a week later, and a misleading map is worse than none: the agent trusts it and skips the search that would have corrected it. The generator is a small deterministic script (the repo's own tooling, no new dependency), it is regenerated by the pre-commit hook, and `verify` fails on a stale index. Staleness must be a red gate, not a convention.

**Put in it exactly what decides "open this file or not":**

- one entry per module, at a fixed heading so the agent can jump by path;
- what it **exports**, and for every function its **input and output** — parameter names plus the return type from the type annotations the repo already keeps. A bare name says a symbol exists; a signature says whether it is the one being looked for, and that is the difference between one file opened and five;
- what it **subscribes to** — `emitter.on('event')` wiring, which an import list structurally cannot show, and which is often the real contract of a module;
- what it **imports** and **who imports it**, so a change's blast radius is visible without a search.

**Leave out what does not earn context:** tests, fixtures, generated trees, build output, vendored code. Do not embed full doc comments; the index says which file to open, the file says the rest. Cap long types with an ellipsis rather than letting one signature eat a screen.

**State its cost where the agent reads it, and guard that number.** Write the figure into the instruction file: an agent that knows what the index costs can decide whether to read it whole. That figure is a promise like any other and goes stale the first time the index grows, so add a check that compares the stated number against the real one and fails outside a tolerance. A budget number nobody verifies is the exact failure this whole runbook exists to prevent. **Pick the unit before the precision.** Tokens are what the agent actually pays, and a tokenizer gives them exactly only for its own model family (`gpt-tokenizer`/o200k counts OpenAI tokens; Claude, Gemini and Kimi tokenize differently) — and it is a dependency that exists only to measure, and in a repo that keeps its dependency list short that can be a bad trade. Bytes need nothing and are wrong by up to ~20 % in either direction: density varies that much between prose and generated tables. Either is fine and the choice is the user's; what is NOT fine is a token number produced by dividing bytes by four, because it looks like a measurement and is a guess. State the unit next to the number so nobody has to infer it.

**Wire the read-first rule explicitly.** The index only pays off if the agent is told to start there, so put one short paragraph in `AGENTS.md` (and its `.github/copilot-instructions.md` copy) that says: read the index before searching, open only what it names, and fall back to search when the index does not answer. Keep the pointer tiny — the pointer is a fixed cost paid every session, the index is a variable cost paid on demand, and the point is to move weight from the first to the second. Use `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` with `applyTo` to attach per-area pointers automatically, so editing a package brings its own rules without anyone loading them globally.

**Scale it before it stops fitting.** When the index outgrows what is worth reading whole, shard it: one file per package plus a root table of contents naming each shard and its size. The agent reads the table, then one shard. In an Nx workspace, `nx graph` is already the project-level index — complement it with the file-level one, never restate the project graph in prose that will drift from it.

**Anti-patterns**, each of which turns the index from an asset into a liability: a hand-maintained map; an index nobody is told to read; an index of names without signatures (the agent still has to open everything); indexing tests and fixtures; a stated size that no gate checks; regenerating it only in CI, so local commits carry a stale one.

### Project glossary — the words, and what they are called in the code

The index answers WHERE something is. It cannot answer WHAT IT IS CALLED, and that is the other half of every failed search: a person asks about the thing they name in their own language, the code names it something else, and the UI names it a third thing. The agent then greps for a word that appears nowhere, finds nothing, and falls back to reading files — the exact cost the index was built to avoid. A glossary is the mapping between those vocabularies, and it is read at session start next to the index.

**Map in both directions.** Word → identifier lets the agent turn a request into a search. Identifier → word lets it turn a symbol it just read into language the person will recognise in the reply. A one-way list only solves half the sessions. One row is: the term, one line of meaning, the identifiers and paths it lives in, and the synonyms that must NOT be used.

**Include only what the name does not already tell you.** A glossary of every class in the repository is noise that competes with the index for context. Earn a row by being one of:

- a domain word whose identifier is different (the spoken name and `camelCase` name diverge, or prose is in one language and code in another);
- an overloaded word that means two things in two places, with both meanings spelled out and the disambiguator named;
- a word with rejected synonyms, so the agent stops searching for the variant nobody used;
- a concept with no single symbol, where the row's job is to name the two or three files that together implement it;
- an abbreviation or internal coinage that no outside reader could expand.

**Meanings are written by a human, mappings are checked by a gate.** The sentence explaining what a term means cannot be generated and should not be; that is the value. What CAN be verified is every identifier and path a row points at — a gate that resolves each one and fails on a miss turns the glossary from documentation, which rots silently, into a claim, which goes red. Rename a symbol without touching the glossary and the build tells you.

**Keep it next to the index and point at both in one breath.** Same instruction-file paragraph, same read-first rule, both sized in the same unit so the agent can budget. If the glossary and the index disagree about a name, the glossary is the one that changed last and the index is generated — regenerate before believing either.

**Anti-patterns:** a glossary that repeats the index (names without meanings); one that grows into prose documentation and stops being scannable; unverified mappings; rows for terms whose identifier is the obvious translation of the word; two glossaries, one for humans and one for the agent, which guarantees they diverge.

### Node runtime & V8 — every tool runs on it, so this multiplies everything else

- Pin: `.nvmrc` = `engines.node` (single source), strict engines on: npm and pnpm < 11 `engine-strict=true` in `.npmrc`; pnpm ≥ 11 `engineStrict: true` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (check: `pnpm config get engineStrict` prints `true`).
- Compile cache: set `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` to an ABSOLUTE path outside `node_modules`: `<repo>/.cache/node-compile-cache` (add `.cache/` to `.gitignore`; in GitLab CI `$CI_PROJECT_DIR/.cache/node-compile-cache`), or a per-user absolute dir on machines with many repos. Never a relative path (Node resolves it against each process's cwd and scatters caches wherever a script `cd`s), and never inside `node_modules` (`npm ci` deletes `node_modules` first, which wipes both the local cache and the one CI restored). Verify: `node -p "require('node:module').getCompileCacheDir()"` prints the absolute dir, or `undefined` when the cache is off. Node then stores V8 bytecode for every module it loads, so the next start of `nx`, `eslint`, `vitest`, `tsc`, the Angular CLI skips parsing and compiling thousands of files. Check whether the installed Node already enables it by default; if not, set it in `docs/dev-setup.md` (shell profile / Windows user env — it must exist before Node starts, an npm script cannot set it for itself), in CI `variables:`, and make the dir gitignored and CI-cached. Entries are keyed by Node version and flags, so a Node bump just misses once. Measure cold CLI start before/after.
- Young-generation GC: `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-semi-space-size=<n>` (try 32–128 MB; default is small). Build tooling, the TypeScript/Angular compilers and test runners allocate short-lived objects at a rate that triggers scavenges constantly; a larger semi-space means fewer of them. Cost is ~3× the value in RAM per process — pick the smallest value that stops improving `build`/`test` time, set it in `docs/dev-setup.md` and CI, not in scripts. Do not set `--max-old-space-size` globally; raise it only for the one target that actually OOMs, on that target.
- Inherit, don't lose: scripts that spawn Node (`tools/scripts/*.mjs`, Nx executors, Vitest workers) must pass `process.env` through, or the cache and GC settings vanish in child processes.
- Log noise: `NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1` in CI only; never locally (warnings are signal).
- Tie-in: `n/no-unsupported-features/*` rules read `engines.node`, so "built-ins over packages" stays safe exactly for the pinned major.

### VS Code workspace — committed `.vscode/`, DX + Windows perf

Often worth more on Windows than the whole Vitest tuning: an unexcluded watcher on `node_modules` + `.nx` + `.angular` + `dist` keeps the file watcher, search index, tsserver and Defender busy on every build.

- `.vscode/settings.json` (workspace-scoped, committed; personal prefs stay in user settings):
  - `files.watcherExclude`, `search.exclude`, `files.exclude` for `**/node_modules/**`, `**/.nx/**`, `**/.angular/**`, `**/dist/**`, `**/coverage/**`, `**/playwright-report/**`, `**/test-results/**`, `**/blob-report/**`, `**/.eslintcache`, the `<pm>` store dir; `search.followSymlinks: false` (pnpm's `node_modules/.pnpm` symlink forest).
  - TypeScript: `typescript.tsdk: node_modules/typescript/lib` + `typescript.enablePromptUseWorkspaceTsdk: true` (one compiler version everywhere), `typescript.tsserver.maxTsServerMemory` raised for large workspaces, `typescript.preferences.includePackageJsonAutoImports: "off"` (stops tsserver indexing every dependency for auto-imports), tsserver log off. In `tsconfig`: `watchOptions.excludeDirectories` for `node_modules`, `dist`, `.nx`, `.angular`.
  - ESLint: `eslint.useFlatConfig: true`, `eslint.validate` incl. `html` (Angular templates), `eslint.workingDirectories: [{ "mode": "auto" }]` for the monorepo, `eslint.run: "onSave"` when typed linting makes on-type linting laggy, `editor.codeActionsOnSave: { "source.fixAll.eslint": "explicit" }`.
  - Format: the formatter the gate actually runs, and only that one, as `editor.defaultFormatter` — Prettier → `esbenp.prettier-vscode`; oxfmt/oxlint → `oxc.oxc-vscode` + `editor.codeActionsOnSave: { "source.fixAll.oxc": "explicit" }` + `oxc.disableNestedConfig: true` and `oxc.fmt.disableNestedConfig: true` when the scripts pass `--disable-nested-config` (exact list in `/migrate-to-oxc` §8); Biome → `biomejs.biome`. If Markdown is deliberately left unformatted (`**/*.md` in the formatter's ignore list), add `"[markdown]": { "editor.defaultFormatter": null }`. Always `editor.formatOnSave: true`, `files.eol: "\n"` (matches `.gitattributes`), and never `source.organizeImports` next to an import sorter (ESLint rule or formatter).
  - Task/scan noise in monorepos: `npm.autoDetect: "off"`, `typescript.tsc.autoDetect: "off"`.
  - Copilot: `.github/prompts/*.prompt.md` and `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` are discovered by default, so do not add `chat.promptFilesLocations` or `chat.instructionsFilesLocations`. Both are deprecated and only used by the Local agent, which VS Code is removing. If the repo already sets them only to those default folders, delete them. `.github/copilot-instructions.md` is controlled by `github.copilot.chat.codeGeneration.useInstructionFiles` and `AGENTS.md` by `chat.useAgentsMdFile`. Both default to `true`, so set them only if a user or org setting turned them off. Prompt files are not loaded by Agent Host sessions. Before committing, check every id against the installed VS Code build's settings reference.
  - Vitest / Playwright extensions: point them at the repo configs; disable continuous background runs if they compete for CPU with the terminal.
- `.vscode/extensions.json`: `recommendations` = Angular Language Service, the extensions of the linters/formatters the repo actually runs (ESLint and/or oxc; Prettier or Biome — only those present), Vitest, Playwright, EditorConfig, Copilot + Copilot Chat, Nx Console only if the team uses it; `unwantedRecommendations` = every formatter/linter extension the repo does NOT run (e.g. `esbenp.prettier-vscode` in an oxfmt repo, `biomejs.biome` in a Prettier repo) plus TSLint-era and Beautify-style extensions.
- Verify every setting id against the installed VS Code / extension versions before committing; measure with the VS Code "Developer: Show Running Extensions" and tsserver restart time before/after.

### Package manager — common (all three)

- Pin the manager: `packageManager` field in `package.json` (the version lives there and nowhere else). Pick the bootstrap line by Node major (`node --version`): Node ≤ 24 → `corepack enable`. Node ≥ 25 ships no Corepack, so: pnpm → `npm i -g pnpm@<version from packageManager>` (pnpm ≥ 11 then switches itself to the declared version, `pmOnFail: download`); Yarn Berry → `npm i -g corepack && corepack enable`; npm → nothing. Write that one line in `docs/dev-setup.md` and use the same line in CI `before_script`. Never type a version in prose.
- Lockfile always committed; frozen installs everywhere except an explicit `deps:update` script.
- Kill install noise in CI and hooks: disable audit, fund, progress and update-notifier via the manager's config file (npm and pnpm < 11: `.npmrc`; pnpm ≥ 11: `pnpm-workspace.yaml`; Yarn Berry: `.yarnrc.yml`), not via ad-hoc flags in scripts.
- Prefer offline/cached resolution locally and in CI.
- Dedupe + pin duplicated transitive deps (`overrides` in `package.json` for npm, top-level `overrides:` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` for pnpm ≥ 11, `resolutions` for Yarn), and add a `deps:check` script to `verify` = duplicate check + `knip` + Nx Cloud grep. The duplicate check and `knip` start as a warning and become a blocker once clean; the Nx Cloud grep blocks from its first commit (rule 4). Duplicate check per manager: pnpm `pnpm dedupe --check`, Yarn Berry `yarn dedupe --check`, Yarn Classic `yarn-deduplicate --list --fail`. npm has no failing check (`npm dedupe --check` is rejected as an unknown flag), so on npm run `npm find-dupes` as a report only; it never blocks.
- Production installs (Docker/deploy) omit dev dependencies.

#### npm

- Install: `npm ci --prefer-offline` (audit/fund/progress off via `.npmrc`: `audit=false`, `fund=false`, `progress=false`, `update-notifier=false`).
- `npm dedupe` once; `npm find-dupes` (report only, never blocks) in `deps:check`; `overrides` for stragglers; `npm ci --omit=dev` for prod images.
- CI cache: set `npm_config_cache` to a repo-local dir (e.g. `.npm/`) and cache it keyed on `package-lock.json`.
- Optional, verify first: `--ignore-scripts` in CI if no dependency needs `postinstall`.

#### pnpm

- Install: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline`.
- Config location depends on the major version. Run `pnpm --version` first. pnpm ≥ 11: every setting goes in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` in camelCase (`nodeLinker`, `shamefullyHoist`, `autoInstallPeers`, `dedupePeerDependents`, `preferFrozenLockfile`, `storeDir`). `.npmrc` is read for auth/registry only, and the `pnpm` field of `package.json` is ignored without an error. pnpm ≤ 10: `.npmrc` and the `pnpm` field of `package.json` still work.
- Keep `nodeLinker: isolated` and strictness as-is (no `shamefullyHoist` unless already present). `autoInstallPeers`, `dedupePeerDependents` and `preferFrozenLockfile` default to true. Only check that nobody set them to false, and verify each against the installed pnpm version.
- Lifecycle scripts: pnpm blocks dependency build scripts by default. Allowlist only what truly needs them. pnpm ≥ 11: the `allowBuilds:` map in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (e.g. `esbuild: true`). pnpm ≤ 10: `onlyBuiltDependencies`. Take candidates from the "Ignored build scripts" warning pnpm prints at install, never from memory.
- `pnpm dedupe` once, `pnpm dedupe --check` in `deps:check`; for stragglers use top-level `overrides:` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (pnpm ≥ 11) or `pnpm.overrides` in `package.json` (pnpm ≤ 10).
- CI cache: `storeDir: .pnpm-store` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (pnpm ≤ 10: `store-dir` in `.npmrc`), cached keyed on `pnpm-lock.yaml`; `pnpm store prune` in a scheduled job, not on every run.
- Docker: `pnpm fetch` on the lockfile layer, then `pnpm install --offline` — dependency layer survives source changes.
- Windows gotcha: hardlinks need store and repos on the same volume — on a Dev Drive put the store (`storeDir` / `store-dir`) on that drive too.

#### Yarn — detect Classic vs Berry, do not migrate

- Classic: `yarn install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline`; `yarn-deduplicate` once (`--list --fail` in `deps:check`; without `--fail` it always exits 0); `resolutions` for stragglers; CI cache: `--cache-folder .yarn-cache/` keyed on `yarn.lock`; disable progress/emoji noise in `.yarnrc`.
- Berry: `yarn install --immutable` (add `--immutable-cache` only when the cache is committed); keep the existing `nodeLinker` and zero-install choice untouched; `yarn dedupe` once, `yarn dedupe --check` in `deps:check`; `resolutions` for stragglers; verify `compressionLevel` and `enableGlobalCache` for the installed version and pick what makes CI cache smaller/faster; CI cache: `.yarn/cache` (if not committed) keyed on `yarn.lock`; `yarn workspaces focus` for CI jobs that need one project only.

### Nx — local cache + affected, never Nx Cloud

- Remove Nx Cloud if present (one commit): `nx-cloud` dependency, `nxCloudId` / `nxCloudAccessToken` / cloud `tasksRunnerOptions` in `nx.json`, `NX_CLOUD_*` in CI and env files, cloud-related scripts. Add `neverConnectToCloud: true`, `NX_NO_CLOUD=true` in CI variables and `.env.example`, and the `deps:check` grep guard. Note: custom task runners are not a substitute — do not add community remote-cache runners either.
- `verify` and pre-push run `nx affected -t lint typecheck test build` (+ `e2e` only when the app is affected). Keep full `run-many` as `verify:all`. `defaultBase` in `nx.json` = the default branch.
- `targetDefaults`: `cache: true` for `build`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, `e2e`; `build.dependsOn: ["^build"]`; `test.inputs: ["default", "^production", {…test configs…}]`; `lint.inputs` include the ESLint config files; `outputs` exact (`{projectRoot}/dist`, `{workspaceRoot}/coverage/{projectRoot}`, `{workspaceRoot}/playwright-report`…) — verify a warm run actually restores them.
- `namedInputs`: `default` = `{projectRoot}/**/*` + `sharedGlobals`; `production` excludes specs, test setup, `*.md`, `docs/**`, e2e, tool configs; `sharedGlobals` only files that truly affect every project and that Nx does not hash already: the root tsconfig and the Node version (`{ "runtime": "node --version" }` or `.nvmrc`). Never the lockfile — Nx already hashes external dependency versions, so a lockfile entry turns every dependency bump into a cache miss for every project; if `sharedGlobals` already lists the lockfile, remove it. Not the whole root either.
- Parallelism: `parallel` in `nx.json` ≈ physical cores locally; in CI set per runner size.
- Daemon on for interactive `nx` commands locally (`NX_DAEMON` unset); `NX_DAEMON=false` in CI. Any script or hook that loads the project graph itself (`createProjectGraphAsync` from `@nx/devkit`) sets `process.env.NX_DAEMON = 'false'` before loading it: a daemon started by that script inherits its stdout and keeps the pipe open, so `pnpm lint | …`, lint-staged and CI hang until the daemon dies (app-factory `tools/scripts/arch-boundaries.mjs`: a 10-minute hang). `cacheDirectory` = `.nx/cache` (gitignored) so GitLab can cache it.
- Graph hygiene: a module-boundary gate with tags — `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` when ESLint lints JS/TS, the boundaries gate from `/migrate-to-oxc` §7 when oxlint does (Step 0 under "ESLint — quality plugins" decides which); keep plugins' inferred tasks or explicit targets consistently (not both for the same target); use plugin `include`/`exclude` to shrink graph computation in large repos. Cross-project imports are caught by that gate (the `lint` target), never by `nx graph --file=…`, which only writes the graph and never fails, so it is not a check.
- Diagnose cache misses with `<pm> exec nx show target <project>:<target> inputs` (and `--check <file>` for one file) before touching inputs; `--verbose` prints stack traces, not input hashes. `nx reset` only when the daemon/graph is corrupted.
- Cross-project asset copies (a host app bundling remotes' outputs; verified on app-factory 2026-09-17): a target whose `assets` glob points INTO other projects' `dist/` races with the parallel builds rewriting those dirs — `ENOENT lstat/copyfile …/chunk-….js` naming a file of an INNOCENT project, flaky, blamed on the host. Rules: (1) copy only what is consumed (`glob: "*-element/**/*"`, never `**/*` over all of `dist/apps`); (2) order it — `dependsOn: [{ "projects": [<producers>], "target": "build-element" }, "^build"]`; a project-level `dependsOn` REPLACES `targetDefaults`, so repeat `^build`; (3) `dependsOn` is a task-graph edge, not a project-graph one — the host's cache hash ignores the producers' outputs until `inputs` adds `{ "dependentTasksOutputFiles": "**/*", "transitive": false }`; a project-level `inputs` REPLACES `targetDefaults` exactly like `dependsOn`, so copy the host target's `inputs` from `targetDefaults` in `nx.json` and append the object — e.g. `"inputs": ["production", "^production", { "dependentTasksOutputFiles": "**/*", "transitive": false }]` (prove it: touch one producer source → exactly that producer + the host re-run; touch one host source → the host re-runs); (4) the path the host loads at runtime must match the emitted layout — `@angular/build:application` writes to `<outputPath>/browser/`, so a loader asking for `<dir>/main.js` 404s on every remote while every build is green (app-factory shipped that for two months); assert the contract in a guard script wired into `verify` (producer list == loader list == `dependsOn`; `dependsOn` still has `^build` and `inputs` still has `production` and `^production`; loader path template vs `outputPath` layout) because no gate runs the browser; (5) state the cost: the host's uncached build now includes its producers (15 → 28 tasks, ~30 s → ~55 s at `parallel: 5`), cached runs unchanged.

### Angular

- Builders: `@angular/build:application`, `@angular/build:dev-server`, `@angular/build:unit-test` (Vitest) — migrate if still on legacy `browser`/Karma; keep `.angular/cache` enabled; `cli.analytics: false` (`NG_CLI_ANALYTICS=false` in CI).
- Zoneless: read the `@angular/core` major from `package.json`. v21+: zoneless is already the default — search for `provideZoneChangeDetection(` and, if the app already runs OnPush + signals, remove it and drop `zone.js` / `zone.js/testing` from `polyfills` (build and test targets) and from deps; `provideZonelessChangeDetection()` is optional there. v20: add `provideZonelessChangeDetection()` and drop `zone.js` the same way. Either way, if the app is not ready, write it as a recommendation with the blockers listed.
- Schematics defaults in `angular.json` (Nx: `nx.json` → `generators`): `skipTests: false`; add `standalone: true` and `changeDetection: OnPush` only below Angular v22 (the `@angular/core` major read above; v22 already defaults both) — so new code is born fast.
- Routing: lazy `loadComponent` / `loadChildren` per feature; a preloading strategy (`PreloadAllModules` or quicklink-style) only if it measurably helps; `@defer` for heavy below-the-fold blocks; `NgOptimizedImage` for images.
- Build hygiene: `budgets` enforced in prod, `outputHashing: all`, prod source maps off or hidden, `optimization` on; dev configuration: no optimization, source maps only where useful.
- Tree-shaking killers: no deep barrel `index.ts` chains (import from the file), no whole-library imports (`lodash`, `moment`, full Material entrypoints); `sideEffects: false` in library `package.json`; check with `--stats-json` + `esbuild-visualizer`.
- TS: `strict`, `strictTemplates`, `isolatedModules: true`, `skipLibCheck: true`.
- Tests: add `provideZonelessChangeDetection()` in `TestBed` only while the test target still loads `zone.js` / `zone.js/testing` (v21+ without zone.js: TestBed is already zoneless); pure logic (services, `computed`, utils) tested without `TestBed`; override heavy children (`TestBed.overrideComponent`) instead of rendering trees; `provideRouter([])` / `provideHttpClientTesting()` over module imports; harnesses only where they pay for themselves.
- SSR/hydration only if the app already uses `@angular/ssr`: `provideClientHydration(withEventReplay())`, incremental hydration on `@defer` blocks — otherwise out of scope.

### Vitest

- Pool: `pool: 'threads'` + `isolate: false` — only if the full suite passes twice in a row and once with `sequence.shuffle: true`; otherwise keep isolation and document why. `pool: 'vmThreads'` only for memory-bound suites.
- `maxWorkers` ≈ physical cores locally, explicit per runner size in CI; `fileParallelism: true`.
- Environments: `node` by default; `jsdom` only where DOM is needed — split with `test.projects` (or per-file `// @vitest-environment` pragma) so pure logic never pays for jsdom startup. Keep `setupFiles` tiny; no heavy global imports.
- `include` narrowed to `src/**/*.spec.ts`; `exclude` `node_modules`, `dist`, `.nx`, `.angular`, e2e dirs.
- Determinism: `restoreMocks: true`, `clearMocks: true`, fake timers for time-based logic, msw for HTTP, `retry: 0` locally (never hide flakes), `bail: 1` in CI.
- Coverage: `provider: 'v8'`, `include` = sources only, `exclude` specs/configs/barrels, `thresholds` (≥80 % lines/branches/functions) as the gate, reporters `text-summary` + `lcov` + `cobertura` (GitLab MR diff coverage); coverage only in `verify`/CI, never in watch.
- Reporters: `default` locally; `dot` + `junit` (`outputFile`) in CI for GitLab `reports: junit`.
- Type checking via `tsc --noEmit` in `typecheck`, not `vitest --typecheck`.
- Scripts: `test` = `vitest run`, `test:watch` = `vitest`, `test:changed` = `vitest run --changed`, `test:cov` = `vitest run --coverage`.
- CI sharding for large suites: `vitest run --shard=$CI_NODE_INDEX/$CI_NODE_TOTAL --reporter=blob` under `parallel:`. Save the blob directory as `artifacts: paths:` of the shard jobs. The directory depends on the installed Vitest: 5.x writes `.vitest/blob/`, 4.x writes `.vitest-reports/`. Check `vitest --version` first. If `outputFile` in the config is a plain string (for example the junit path), change it to the object form `outputFile: { junit: '...' }`. Otherwise the blob reporter writes into that file instead of the directory. Then run `vitest --merge-reports=<that dir>` in a follow-up job with `needs:` on the shard jobs. Add the blob directory to `.gitignore`.
- Timeouts explicit (`testTimeout`, `hookTimeout`) — slow tests fail loudly, not silently.

### TypeScript

- `incremental: true`, `tsBuildInfoFile` in a gitignored dir, `skipLibCheck: true`. `typecheck` depends on the layout:
  - One tsconfig, no `references`: `typecheck` = `tsc --noEmit -p <tsconfig>`.
  - Several projects: use project references. Put `composite: true` in each referenced project's tsconfig, with `outDir` / `tsBuildInfoFile` in a gitignored dir. Add a root solution tsconfig (`"files": []` + `"references": [...]`). Then `typecheck` = `tsc -b <root solution tsconfig>`. Do not use `tsc --noEmit -p` on a project that has `references`. On a clean tree it fails with TS6305 ("Output file ... has not been built from source file") before any real type error, because `-p` does not build the referenced projects and `-b` does.

### Formatter — `nx format` vs Prettier vs Biome vs oxfmt (default is the one already there)

Swapping the formatter touches every file in the repository and is a matter of taste as much as of speed, so it is one of the few items on this list that you **must put to the user before doing**. Measure first, then ask, then implement only a yes. The exception is the Nx default below, which is not a swap at all.

**In an Nx workspace the default is `nx format`, and you do not need to ask to adopt it, provided it resolves to the formatter the repo already uses.** Nx ships `nx format:check` and `nx format:write`. They take the same `--base` / `--projects` / `--files` targeting as the rest of Nx, so `verify` and the pre-push hook check only what changed instead of the whole tree. Which formatter they run depends on the installed Nx, so check it before wiring anything. Open `node_modules/nx/dist/src/utils/formatters/index.js` and read `detectFormatter`. If that file is missing, the installed Nx is older and formats with Prettier only. In Nx 23.2 the order is:

1. An oxfmt config at the root (`.oxfmtrc.json`, `.oxfmtrc.jsonc`, `oxfmt.config.ts`, `oxfmt.config.mts`) → oxfmt.
2. Otherwise a Prettier config file or a `prettier` key in `package.json` → Prettier.
3. Otherwise an `oxfmt` dependency in the root `package.json`, then a `prettier` dependency.
4. Otherwise nothing.

Biome is never detected. With no formatter detected, `nx format:check` prints 'No formatter configured.' and exits 0. In a Biome repo, or one with no formatter, do NOT wire `nx format` into `verify`: that gate would always pass. Keep the repo's own formatter command instead. When the detected formatter is the one already installed, this is the same win as a faster binary, obtained with **zero new dependencies and zero new configuration**: no second formatter in `package.json`, no second config file, no second ignore file, no second editor extension, no second entry in CI caching. Wire `format` to `nx format:write` and `format:check` to `nx format:check`, with no `--base` in the script: Nx takes the base from `NX_BASE` (set by the pre-push hook and the MR pipeline, see "Git hooks" and "GitLab CI"), else from `defaultBase` in `nx.json`, and takes the merge-base with HEAD itself. Do not write `$(git merge-base ...)` into the script: on Windows pnpm and npm run scripts through cmd.exe, which leaves `$(...)` unexpanded. In CI on the default branch run `nx format:check --all` instead. Without `--all`, Nx checks only files changed since the merge-base plus uncommitted and untracked files, and on the default branch that is nothing. Then stop there.

Only when Nx is absent, when `nx format` detects no formatter (Biome or none), or when the user asks for the comparison explicitly, is the four-way question live. For the oxfmt route, measure and ask as below; a yes is implemented by `/migrate-to-oxc`, not by the Biome steps below:

|             | covers                                                                                      | new dependencies                        | new configuration                                             | speed                                                 |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `nx format` | whatever the detected formatter covers (oxfmt, else Prettier; Biome is never detected) | none, if oxfmt or Prettier is already installed | none | only changed files |
| Prettier    | `.ts`, `.js`, `.html` (Angular templates included), `.css`/`.scss`, `.json`, `.md`, `.yaml` | the one already installed               | the one already written                                       | `--cache` makes a warm run cheap                      |
| Biome       | `.ts`, `.js`, `.json`, `.css`; `.html` only after enabling it explicitly; **no Markdown**   | one binary, plus a new editor extension | `biome.jsonc`, new ignore syntax, editor formatter re-pointed | about 4× faster than Prettier cold on a JS-only tree; slower than oxfmt (copilot-builder: 1.7 s vs 0.4 s wall, same tree) |
| oxfmt       | Prettier's coverage and output (Angular control flow, `.md`, `.yaml` included)              | one binary, plus a new editor extension | `.oxfmtrc.jsonc`; reads `.gitignore` and `.prettierignore`    | fastest measured: about 0.4 s wall on a small repo; compare wall time, not oxfmt's own `Finished in N ms` line |

- **Measure both on this repo's own files**, not on a blog's benchmark: full check cold and warm for the current formatter, then the same file set through `npx @biomejs/biome format .`. If oxfmt is the candidate, measure it the same way: `npx oxfmt --check .` (wall time, cold and warm), and `npx oxfmt --list-different .` on a scratch copy for the disagreement count. Report wall time and, more importantly, **how many files the two disagree about** (`biome format --write` on a scratch copy, then `git diff --stat`). A one-line diff and a ten-thousand-line diff are different decisions.
- **Check what Biome does not cover, against the installed version, not against this text.** Read the shipped schema (`node_modules/@biomejs/biome/configuration_schema.json`) and list its language sections. At the time of writing there is no `markdown` section, so every `.md` file in the repo would lose its formatting gate — in a docs-heavy repo that is the whole decision. Its HTML formatter is off by default and young, which matters most in Angular repos, where templates are half the code. Biome already parses comments in well-known JSONC files (`tsconfig*.json`, `jsconfig.json`, `.vscode/*.json`, `.eslintrc.json`) with no configuration; do not add a setting for them. For any other `.json` file that carries comments, run `npx @biomejs/biome format <file>` without a config: a parse error means that file needs `json.parser.allowComments: true` (scoped with `overrides` to those files), or the formatter will reject it as malformed.
- **A Biome plugin does not close a language gap** — do not let "it is extensible" end the discussion. Plugins are GritQL patterns matched against a tree Biome itself parsed, they are lint-only (so they do nothing under `linter.enabled: false` or `biome format`), and they never emit formatting. A file type Biome cannot parse never reaches them: with a plugin configured, `biome check x.md` still answers "these paths were provided but ignored". Verify that on the installed binary before either believing or repeating it.
- **oxfmt closes Biome's language gap, so check what it would ADD, not only what it keeps.** `npx oxfmt --migrate prettier` (or `biome`) writes `.oxfmtrc.json` from the old config; the CLI always writes `.oxfmtrc.json`; rename it to `.oxfmtrc.jsonc` if you want `//` comments in it (oxfmt finds either name without `--config`), and keep exactly one of the two files; verify the ignore list by hand — in one migration Biome's `!!` "do not crawl" entries did not survive it. Then `--list-different` on a scratch copy and read the diff by file type: by default oxfmt sorts `package.json` keys (`sortPackageJson: false` to keep manifests), adds trailing commas to `.jsonc`, and formats Markdown — which pads every table to its widest cell (one measured AGENTS.md went from 11,349 to 16,761 bytes, +48 %; measure the target repo's own instruction files, the growth differs per repo) and inserts blank lines inside HTML-comment markers. In a repo whose prose is read by agents, that is a token cost to put in the question, and `**/*.md` in `ignorePatterns` is the answer that keeps it out.
- **Ask the user in one question with the numbers in it**: how much time is saved, how many files change, which file types stop being formatted, how many dependencies and config files appear, and what the fallback is (keep Prettier with `--cache`, which is usually within a factor of two of Biome on a warm run). Offer the hybrid explicitly — Biome for code, Prettier kept for Markdown only — because it is the option that loses nothing and is easy to miss, and say plainly that it means maintaining two formatters.
- **If the answer is yes for Biome**, it is a formatter swap and nothing else: carry the existing numbers over verbatim (line width, quote style, trailing commas, line ending, indent), set `linter.enabled: false` and `assist.enabled: false` so a bundled linter and import sorter do not rewrite files nobody asked to change, translate the ignore file into `files.includes` with `!` negations, remove the old formatter from the manifest, config and editor settings (`editor.defaultFormatter`, recommended extensions), and regenerate anything that embeds line numbers. Point `$schema` at the copy in `node_modules` so the version is not declared a second time. In an Nx workspace also set `NX_SKIP_FORMAT=true`, because Nx formats generated files only with Prettier or oxfmt and would otherwise keep running Prettier over files the repo no longer formats with it.
- **If the answer is yes for oxfmt**, stop here and run `/migrate-to-oxc`: §0, §1, §2 and §8 (formatter, hooks, editor, CI, generator). Run §3-§7 only if the user also said yes to the linter. Do **not** set `NX_SKIP_FORMAT`: Nx generators format with oxfmt natively when an oxfmt config (`.oxfmtrc.json` or `.oxfmtrc.jsonc`) exists, and the variable would turn that formatting off.
- **If the answer is no**, the cheap win is `--cache` when the existing formatter is Prettier (oxfmt 0.68 has no cache option; it is already fast enough without one), plus making sure the cache directory is gitignored (or lives under `node_modules`) and restored in CI.
- Either way, adopting Biome's or oxc's **linter** (oxlint) is a separate question from adopting its formatter. Do not bundle them: the linter's findings are a code-review backlog, not a formatting change, and mixing the two makes the diff unreviewable.

### ESLint — performance

- Flat config only; `eslint --cache --cache-location .eslintcache` (gitignored) locally and in lint-staged; in CI add `--cache-strategy content` (a fresh clone gives every file a new mtime, so the default `metadata` strategy would re-lint everything) and restore `.eslintcache` from the GitLab tooling cache.
- Typed linting is the expensive part: `parserOptions.projectService: true` (no hand-listed `project` arrays), typed configs applied only to `**/*.ts` sources, `disableTypeChecked` for `*.js`, `*.mjs`, config and spec-helper files; keep `allowDefaultProject` minimal.
- Find slow rules with `TIMING=1 <pm> exec eslint .` (bash / Git Bash; PowerShell: `$env:TIMING='1'; <pm> exec eslint .; Remove-Item Env:TIMING`); restrict the known heavy ones (`import-x/no-cycle` with `maxDepth`, `sonarjs/cognitive-complexity` only on sources). When typed ESLint rules dominate `lint` time, the bigger lever is moving the non-Angular rules to oxlint. That is `/migrate-to-oxc` (ask first), not a tweak here.
- Multithreaded linting (`--concurrency`) if the installed ESLint supports it — verify; otherwise parallelism comes from Nx running `lint` per project.
- The formatter chosen in the Formatter section (the one already there: Prettier, oxfmt or Biome) runs separately (lint-staged + `format:check` in `verify`); never through `eslint-plugin-prettier`. Only when that formatter is Prettier: `eslint-config-prettier` is the last entry in the config array. With oxfmt or Biome, do not add Prettier or `eslint-config-prettier`; in an oxfmt repo follow `/migrate-to-oxc`.
- Gate: `--max-warnings 0` in `verify`/CI, `linterOptions.reportUnusedDisableDirectives: 'error'`; every `eslint-disable` needs a `-- reason` (enforced by the comments plugin).

### ESLint — quality plugins (tiered; install only what the repo lacks)

**Step 0 — which linter owns JS/TS.** Run `git ls-files | grep -E '(^|/)(\.oxlintrc|oxlint\.config\.)'`. If it prints anything, oxlint owns JS/TS and ESLint is Angular-only (see `/migrate-to-oxc` §4). In that case:

- Do NOT install any package from the tiers or the layering below into ESLint.
- Keep `eslint.config.mjs` as it is: for `.ts`, an explicit list of `@angular-eslint/*` rules (not `tsRecommended`); for `.html`, `templateRecommended` + `templateAccessibility`; no JS/TS rule from outside Angular.
- Read the tiers only as a checklist of RULES. For each rule, open the oxlint config (`oxlint.rules.mts` and `oxlint.plugins.mts`, or `.oxlintrc.json`). If the rule is already there, skip it. If it is missing, add it to oxlint:
  - through a native oxlint plugin (`typescript`, `unicorn`, `import`, `vitest`, `jsdoc`, `promise`, `node`);
  - or as a `jsPlugins` entry, which is verified only for `eslint-plugin-sonarjs`, `-playwright` and `-security`. Any other plugin must first pass the scratch test in `/migrate-to-oxc` §3 item 6. If it fails, write the rule into `NOT_IN_OXLINT` with a reason (no such list: name it in the report).
- Module boundaries: use the gate from `/migrate-to-oxc` §7 (`no-restricted-imports` layers without Nx, the `arch-boundaries` gate with Nx), not `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries`.
- Then go straight to "Rollout" below (it covers oxlint too) and continue with "Git hooks".

If the grep prints nothing, ESLint is the only JS/TS linter, and the tiers, layering and rollout below apply as written.

Tier 1 — must-have in every repo of this stack:

- `typescript-eslint` → `strictTypeChecked` + `stylisticTypeChecked`. Non-negotiable rules at `error`: `no-explicit-any`, `no-floating-promises`, `no-misused-promises`, `switch-exhaustiveness-check`, `no-unnecessary-condition`, `strict-boolean-expressions`, `consistent-type-imports`, `no-deprecated` (replaces `eslint-plugin-deprecation`), `prefer-readonly`, `explicit-module-boundary-types` on public APIs, `restrict-template-expressions`, `no-unnecessary-type-assertion`.
- Angular presets — pick ONE source, never both. In an Nx repo: `@nx/eslint-plugin` `flat/angular` (it already contains `angular-eslint` `tsRecommended` and the `processInlineTemplates` processor) + `flat/angular-template` (it already contains `templateRecommended` + `templateAccessibility`). Without Nx: `angular-eslint` `tsRecommended` + `templateRecommended` + `templateAccessibility`, with `processInlineTemplates`. On top of whichever preset you chose, turn on as overrides: `prefer-signals`, `prefer-standalone`, `prefer-on-push-component-change-detection`, `prefer-inject`, `no-async-lifecycle-method`, `component-selector` / `directive-selector` with the repo prefix; template: `prefer-control-flow`, `prefer-self-closing-tags`, `no-call-expression`, `button-has-type`, `prefer-ngsrc`, `no-negated-async`, and the accessibility set (`alt-text`, `click-events-have-key-events`, `interactive-supports-focus`, `label-has-associated-control`, `role-has-required-aria`).
- `@nx/eslint-plugin` (Nx repos only) → `flat/base` (it only registers the `@nx` plugin; do NOT add `flat/typescript`: it is typescript-eslint `recommended` with `no-explicit-any` at `warn` and `explicit-module-boundary-types` off, plus `eslint-config-prettier` whenever Prettier is installed, so it loosens the typescript-eslint bullet above) plus the Angular presets from the previous bullet; `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` with `depConstraints` by tags (`type:*`, `scope:*`), and `@nx/dependency-checks` on every publishable/library `package.json`.
- `eslint-plugin-rxjs-x` (the maintained, flat-config successor of `eslint-plugin-rxjs`): `no-ignored-subscription`, `no-nested-subscribe`, `no-unsafe-takeuntil`, `no-ignored-error`, `prefer-observer`, `no-subject-value` — RxJS only at the I/O edge.
- `@vitest/eslint-plugin` on spec files: `expect-expect`, `no-focused-tests` (error), `no-disabled-tests` (error, or off — decide per repo once; warn is not an option under `--max-warnings 0`), `no-identical-title`, `valid-title`, `prefer-to-be`, `consistent-test-it`, `no-standalone-expect`.
- `eslint-plugin-playwright` on e2e files: `recommended` + `no-wait-for-timeout`, `no-focused-test`, `missing-playwright-await`, `prefer-web-first-assertions`, `no-conditional-in-test`, `expect-expect`, `no-networkidle`.
- `@eslint-community/eslint-plugin-eslint-comments`: `require-description`, `no-unlimited-disable`, `disable-enable-pair`. Do not turn on `no-unused-disable`: it is deprecated, and `linterOptions.reportUnusedDisableDirectives: 'error'` (see Gate above) already reports unused disables.
- `eslint-config-prettier` — last, only when the repo's formatter is Prettier (see ESLint — performance).

Tier 2 — strongly recommended:

- `eslint-plugin-unicorn` → `recommended`, then disable the noisy opinion rules (`prevent-abbreviations`, `no-null`, `no-array-reduce` — decide per repo, once); keep `prefer-node-protocol`, `filename-case` (kebab-case), `prefer-top-level-await`, `no-useless-undefined`, `prefer-string-slice`, `throw-new-error`.
- `eslint-plugin-sonarjs` → `recommended`; `cognitive-complexity` at 15, `no-duplicate-string`, `no-identical-functions`, `no-nested-template-literals`. If a SonarQube quality gate exists, align thresholds with it — one standard, not two.
- `eslint-plugin-import-x` + `eslint-import-resolver-typescript`: `no-duplicates`, `no-extraneous-dependencies`, `no-cycle` (scoped, `maxDepth`), `first`, `newline-after-import`; ordering by `eslint-plugin-simple-import-sort` (or `perfectionist` — pick one, never both).
- `eslint-plugin-n` for Node code (tools, scripts, MCP servers): `no-unsupported-features/node-builtins` and `es-syntax` driven by `engines.node` (this is what makes "built-ins over packages" safe), `no-process-exit`, `no-sync` (error, or off — decide per repo once; warn is not an option under `--max-warnings 0`), `no-path-concat`, `prefer-promises/fs`.
- `eslint-plugin-security` for Node code: `detect-child-process`, `detect-non-literal-fs-filename` (every flagged path must first pass the repo's own path-validation helper, meaning a function that resolves the path and rejects anything outside an allowed root; search the code for one before writing a new one; if the repo has none, add `// eslint-disable-next-line security/detect-non-literal-fs-filename -- <why this path is safe>` at that call site), `detect-eval-with-expression`, `detect-unsafe-regex`; `detect-object-injection` (error, or off — decide per repo once; warn is not an option under `--max-warnings 0`).
- `eslint-plugin-regexp` → `recommended` (ReDoS, unreachable alternatives, needless escapes).
- `eslint-plugin-no-secrets` → `no-secrets` at error on sources, tolerance tuned to avoid false positives on hashes in fixtures.
- `eslint-plugin-promise`: `catch-or-return`, `no-nesting`, `always-return` where `no-floating-promises` does not already cover it.

Tier 3 — situational:

- `eslint-plugin-unused-imports` (autofix removal in lint-staged; `no-unused-vars` still reports).
- `eslint-plugin-tsdoc` / `eslint-plugin-jsdoc` (`require-jsdoc` on exported public APIs of published libraries only).
- `@eslint/json` (+ `jsonc` sorting) for `package.json`, `nx.json`, `angular.json`, `tsconfig*.json`; `@eslint/markdown` for docs.
- `eslint-plugin-compat` with the repo `browserslist` when the app ships to legacy browsers.

Do not add: `eslint-plugin-prettier`, `eslint-plugin-rxjs` (unmaintained), `eslint-plugin-deprecation` (superseded), `eslint-plugin-boundaries` when Nx boundaries are already on, two sorting plugins, or any plugin whose rule set duplicates an existing one — every extra plugin costs lint time; each must earn it in the before/after table.

Config layering (one `eslint.config.mjs` per repo, project overrides only where needed):

1. global `ignores`;
2. base JS (`@eslint/js` recommended) for all files;
3. typed TS layer for `**/*.ts` (typescript-eslint strict + stylistic, unicorn, sonarjs, import-x, comments, regexp, no-secrets, promise);
4. Angular layer for app/lib sources (`angular-eslint` ts rules, rxjs-x, Nx boundaries) and an HTML/inline-template layer (`angular-eslint` template + accessibility);
5. Node layer for `tools/**`, scripts and server code (`n`, `security`);
6. test layers — e2e first: files = the roots of the Nx e2e projects (list them with `<pm> exec nx show projects --type e2e`; usually `apps/*-e2e/**/*.ts`; outside Nx, the Playwright `testDir`) → `eslint-plugin-playwright`. Then unit specs = `**/*.spec.ts` with those same e2e roots in the layer's `ignores` → `@vitest/eslint-plugin`. Do not relax `no-explicit-any` in tests. Check: `<pm> exec eslint --print-config apps/<app>-e2e/src/<file>.spec.ts` shows `playwright/*` rules and no `vitest/*` rules;
7. `disableTypeChecked` for JS/config files;
8. `eslint-config-prettier` — only when the repo's formatter is Prettier (see ESLint — performance).

Verify each plugin's flat-config export name for the installed version before wiring it.

Rollout (the gate is `--max-warnings 0` / oxlint `denyWarnings: true`, so `warn` fails verify exactly like `error` — never stage a rule at `warn`):

1. Enable the new plugin's rules at `error` in one commit.
2. Freeze today's violations in the same commit. ESLint: run `<pm> exec eslint --suppress-rule <plugin/rule> .` for each new rule and commit `eslint-suppressions.json` (only `error` rules are suppressed). oxlint: add an `overrides` entry that sets the rule to `off` for exactly the files that violate it today, and list the files by name, never by glob.
3. `<pm> run verify` must be green before you commit.
4. Fix the frozen violations in dedicated `refactor(lint):` commits. After each one, run `<pm> exec eslint --prune-suppressions .` (or remove the fixed files from the oxlint override) so the frozen list only shrinks.

Never land a config that turns the current branch red.

### Git hooks — native, committed, cross-platform

- Layout: `.githooks/pre-commit`, `.githooks/commit-msg`, `.githooks/pre-push` — POSIX `#!/bin/sh`, `set -e`, executable bit committed (`git update-index --chmod=+x`). Git for Windows ships `sh`, so no `.cmd` wrappers.
- Activation: `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`, run from a tiny deterministic `tools/scripts/setup-hooks.mjs` that is a no-op when `.git` is absent or `CI` is set (so published packages and CI never touch git config). Wire it to `prepare` (npm/pnpm/Yarn Classic) or `postinstall` (Yarn Berry, which does not run `prepare` on install) — verify for the installed manager. Then check whether installs skip lifecycle scripts: npm → `npm config get ignore-scripts`; pnpm → `pnpm config get ignoreScripts` (pnpm ≥ 11 reads it only from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`; `ignore-scripts` in `.npmrc` is ignored there). Yarn Berry's `enableScripts: false` does not skip the root `postinstall`, so nothing to check. If it prints `true`, no install runs `prepare` and hooks stay unarmed: keep the script, add `<pm> run prepare` as a one-time step after the first install in `docs/dev-setup.md`, and if the repo has a doctor script add a warning there when `git config core.hooksPath` is not `.githooks` (skip the check when `.git` is absent or `CI` is set; never make `verify` fail on it, CI has no hooks).
- Contents:
  - pre-commit → the repo's OWN linter and formatter (the ones Phase 1 found; never add a second one here), on staged files only: `<pm> exec lint-staged`, with its config calling those same tools (ESLint repo: `eslint --cache --fix` + the existing formatter; oxc repo: the commands from `/migrate-to-oxc` §8, including `--concurrent false --config package.json`); without lint-staged: `git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR -z | xargs -0 -r <formatter> --check`. If the repo has a generated code index (see "Repository index"), the hook also regenerates it from the staged tree and runs `git add` on it. Target: a few seconds at most.
  - commit-msg → `node_modules/.bin/commitlint --edit "$1"` (npm, pnpm, and Yarn with `nodeLinker: node-modules`); Yarn PnP → `yarn commitlint --edit "$1"`.
  - pre-push → `NX_BASE=origin/<default-branch> <pm> run verify`. Nx reads `NX_BASE` (and `NX_HEAD`) from the environment and computes the merge-base itself, so every `nx affected` / `nx format:check` in a chained `verify` gets the same base. Never append `-- --base=…` to a chained script (only its last command receives it). Run `git fetch origin <default-branch>` first if the hook must be exact.
- npm only: `npm exec` treats every flag after the tool name as its own and fails with `EUNKNOWNCONFIG` (e.g. `--edit`). In any hook, call the tool from `node_modules/.bin/<tool>` or write `npm exec -- <tool> <flags>`. Everywhere else in this prompt, `<pm> exec <tool> <flags>` means `npm exec -- <tool> <flags>` on npm. Test each hook once by hand (`sh .githooks/commit-msg .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG`) before committing it.
- Migration from Husky, if present, in one commit, with hook time measured before and after:
  1. For each `.husky/<hook>` except `.husky/_/`, create `.githooks/<hook>` with this content: line 1 `#!/bin/sh`, line 2 `set -e`, then the old body unchanged. If the body calls a tool by its bare name (for example `lint-staged`), rewrite the call to `<pm> exec <tool>` (npm: see the npm-only bullet above), because Husky put `node_modules/.bin` on PATH and native hooks do not.
  2. Run `git update-index --add --chmod=+x .githooks/<hook>` for each new file. Check that `git ls-files -s .githooks` shows `100755`.
  3. Delete the tracked `.husky/<hook>` files. Remove the `husky` dependency and the `prepare: husky` script, and wire `setup-hooks.mjs` into `prepare` as described above. Keep the lint-staged and commitlint configs unchanged.
  4. Run `node tools/scripts/setup-hooks.mjs`, then delete the leftover `.husky/` folder (only the git-ignored `.husky/_/` wrappers are left). Check that `git config --get core.hooksPath` prints `.githooks`, not `.husky/_`. Do this before measuring hook time.
  5. In the commit body and in `docs/dev-setup.md` write: "after pulling this, run `node tools/scripts/setup-hooks.mjs` (or `<pm> install` when it runs `prepare`), delete the leftover `.husky/` folder, and check that `git config --get core.hooksPath` prints `.githooks`". Reason: existing clones keep `core.hooksPath=.husky/_`, and those wrappers exit 0 when `.husky/<hook>` is missing, so no hook runs and nothing warns. Also write there that `HUSKY=0` no longer skips hooks; the only skip is `--no-verify` (see Bypass).
- Bypass: `git commit --no-verify` / `git push --no-verify` only, for emergencies, and say so in the MR. Document it; never script it. `CI` does not bypass a hook that is already armed. It only stops `setup-hooks.mjs` from arming hooks on CI runners.

### Git repo & local git performance

- `.gitattributes`: `* text=auto eol=lf` (no CRLF churn, stable lint-staged diffs); lockfiles and generated files collapsed in MR diffs (`gitlab-generated=true`, plus `linguist-generated=true` for portability); binaries marked `binary`.
- `.gitignore` complete (see Phase 1 list) — cache dirs must never be committed.
- Documented local config (`docs/dev-setup.md`, not enforced): `core.fsmonitor=true`, `core.untrackedCache=true`, `feature.manyFiles=true`, `git maintenance start` (commit-graph, prefetch, gc in background), `core.longpaths=true` on Windows, `merge.conflictstyle=zdiff3`, `diff.algorithm=histogram`, `rerere.enabled=true`, `pull.rebase=true`, `fetch.prune=true`.
- Large repos only (recommendation): partial clone `--filter=blob:none` for new clones.
- Conventions: Conventional Commits via commitlint (scopes per repo), small commits, branch names `type/slug`; `.gitlab/merge_request_templates/Default.md` with the DoD checklist; `CODEOWNERS` if reviewers are fixed.

### Playwright

- Config: `fullyParallel: true`, `workers` explicit in CI (per runner cores) and default locally, `forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI`, `retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0`, `trace: 'on-first-retry'`, `screenshot: 'only-on-failure'`, `video: 'retain-on-failure'` or off, `preserveOutput: 'failures-only'`, explicit `timeout` / `expect.timeout`, `testIdAttribute` set.
- `webServer`: serve the prebuilt `dist/` (static server or prod dev-server), never a full dev build inside the e2e job; `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI`; sane `timeout`.
- Auth & data: `storageState` produced once by a setup project (project `dependencies`), never login per test; seed data via API/fixtures, not UI; tests independent and order-agnostic (`test.describe.configure({ mode: 'parallel' })`).
- Locators & waits: `getByRole` / `getByTestId`, web-first assertions, zero `waitForTimeout`; tags (`@smoke`) so pre-push can run the smoke subset when the full affected suite is too slow — CI still runs everything.
- Browser matrix: `chromium` only on MR pipelines; `firefox` / `webkit` on the default branch and nightly schedule.
- Reports: `list` locally; `blob` + `junit` in CI. Shard with `--shard=$CI_NODE_INDEX/$CI_NODE_TOTAL` under `parallel:`. Every shard uploads `blob-report/` and `test-results/` with `artifacts: when: always`, because `merge-reports` needs every shard's blob, green shards included. Then a follow-up job with `when: always` and `needs:` on the shard job (so it receives every shard's `blob-report/`) runs `<pm> exec playwright merge-reports --reporter html,junit ./blob-report`. The directory argument is required: without it Playwright reads the current directory and fails with "No report files found". Never use `when: on_failure` on shard artifacts: GitLab has one `artifacts:when` per job, so passing shards would upload nothing.
- Scripts: `e2e` = `playwright test`, `e2e:changed` = `playwright test --only-changed`, `e2e:failed` = `--last-failed`, `e2e:ui` for local debugging.
- Browsers: official Playwright image matching installed `@playwright/test` in CI (`PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1` on install); locally cache browsers, do not reinstall on every `install`.
- Flakes: any test needing `retries` locally is a bug — fix or quarantine with a tag, never raise retries to hide it.

### Deps

- Remove `knip` findings; dedupe with `<pm>`; `overrides`/`resolutions` where justified; built-ins over packages when the package is used for <20 % of its features.

### Windows (docs only)

- Document Dev Drive and Defender exclusions for `node_modules`, `.nx`, `.angular`, `dist`, `.eslintcache`, the `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` dir (`<repo>/.cache/node-compile-cache`, absolute) and the `<pm>` cache/store dir in `docs/dev-setup.md`; how to set `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` / `NODE_OPTIONS` as user environment variables (they must exist before any terminal or VS Code starts); and that the committed `.vscode/settings.json` excludes must stay in sync with this list.

### GitLab CI — create or refactor `.gitlab-ci.yml`

- Skeleton: `workflow: rules` = MR pipelines + default branch + schedules, no duplicate branch/MR pipelines; `default:` block for `image`, `interruptible: true`, `retry: { max: 1, when: [runner_system_failure, stuck_or_timeout_failure] }`, per-job `timeout`; `extends` / `!reference` for shared fragments; optionally `include: project:` a shared template repo so every repo in the organization consumes the same pipeline.
- `image` derived from `.nvmrc` (document the mapping; no version in prose); `before_script`: the bootstrap line from "Package manager — common" (Node ≤ 24 → `corepack enable`; Node ≥ 25 → `npm i -g pnpm@<version from packageManager>` for pnpm, `npm i -g corepack && corepack enable` for Yarn Berry, nothing for npm).
- Variables: `CI=true`, `NX_DAEMON=false`, `NX_NO_CLOUD=true`, `NG_CLI_ANALYTICS=false`, `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1` (non-e2e jobs), `<pm>` cache/store dir → repo-local, `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE: "$CI_PROJECT_DIR/.cache/node-compile-cache"` (absolute, outside `node_modules`; cached), `NODE_OPTIONS: "--max-semi-space-size=<n>"` (the value measured in Phase 0), `NODE_NO_WARNINGS: "1"`, `FF_USE_FASTZIP: "true"`, `CACHE_COMPRESSION_LEVEL: "fastest"`, `ARTIFACT_COMPRESSION_LEVEL: "fastest"`, `GIT_DEPTH` compatible with affected (`0`, or a depth plus explicit fetch of the base SHA).
- Stages: `install` → `check` (lint, typecheck, test — parallel jobs, `needs: [{ job: install, artifacts: false }]`, dependencies come from the deps cache) → `build` → `e2e` (`needs: [build]`, consumes the `dist/` artifact — build once). A job that has `needs:` controls artifact download only with `needs: [{ job: <name>, artifacts: false }]` and never also gets `dependencies:` (GitLab: do not combine `dependencies` with `needs` in the same job). Use `dependencies: []` only on a job without `needs:`.
- Install with the detected manager's frozen + offline mode (see blocks above).
- Caches (separate, so each invalidates independently):
  1. deps: `key: { files: [<lockfile>] }` → manager cache/store dir; `policy: pull-push` in `install`, `pull` elsewhere;
  2. Nx + tooling: ONE cache per job, with its own key. GitLab keeps one archive per key and the last writer wins, so jobs running in parallel must never share a key. `key: tools-<job>-$CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG`, `fallback_keys: [tools-<job>-$CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH]`, `policy: pull-push`, where `<job>` is the job name (`lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, `build`, `e2e`). `paths`: `.nx/cache` and the `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` dir (`.cache/node-compile-cache`) in every job, plus this job's own tool dirs: lint → `.eslintcache`; typecheck → `**/*.tsbuildinfo`; test, build and e2e → `.angular/cache`. Never reuse another job's key. This is the only cross-runner cache (Nx Cloud is forbidden). By default GitLab keeps protected and non-protected caches apart (keys and fallback keys get a `-protected` / `-non_protected` suffix), so an MR pipeline from an unprotected branch started by a Developer usually does NOT fall back to the default branch's cache — measure the MR cache-hit rate in Phase 5 instead of assuming it. Every job except `install` lists exactly two caches: deps (1) and its own `tools-<job>` cache (2).
- MR pipelines: set job variables `NX_BASE: $CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA` and `NX_HEAD: $CI_COMMIT_SHA` (under `rules: if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"`), and have each job run the same package script as locally (`<pm> run lint`, `<pm> run typecheck`, `<pm> run test`, `<pm> run build`, each an `nx affected -t <target>`), so local and CI share one command; default branch: full `run-many`; nightly schedule: full run + full browser matrix + `pnpm store prune` / cache warm-up.
- Playwright job on the official image matching installed `@playwright/test`, with `parallel: N` shards. Shard job: `artifacts: { when: always, paths: [blob-report/, test-results/], expire_in: 1 day }`. Merge job: `stage: e2e` (or a later stage), `when: always`, `needs: [<shard job>]` (this waits for all shards and downloads their blobs), script `<pm> exec playwright merge-reports --reporter html,junit ./blob-report`, `artifacts: { when: always, paths: [playwright-report/], reports: { junit: <junit file written by merge-reports> }, expire_in: 1 day }`. Set the junit file name with `PLAYWRIGHT_JUNIT_OUTPUT_NAME`.
- Test/coverage reports: `artifacts.reports.junit` from Vitest and Playwright junit outputs; `artifacts.reports.coverage_report: { coverage_format: cobertura, path: … }`; job-level `coverage:` regex matching the `text-summary` line.
- Gates: `allow_failure: false` on lint/typecheck/test/build/e2e; project settings "pipelines must succeed" + auto-cancel redundant pipelines documented in `docs/dev-setup.md`. Also document the setting Settings > CI/CD > General pipelines > "Use separate caches for protected branches". Clearing it lets MR pipelines reuse the default branch's `.nx/cache`, but GitLab calls the separation a security feature to disable only when every Developer is highly trusted (cache poisoning). This is the owner's decision: put the measured MR cache-hit rate and the trade-off in the report and ask. Never change the setting yourself.
- Optional, off the MR critical path (default branch / schedule only): GitLab SAST and Dependency Scanning templates via `include: template:`.
- No secrets needed for build/test; masked/protected variables only for anything else. No publish/release job. Validate the file with the pipeline editor / CI lint before committing.

## Phase 4 — Review

Every changed file: `| File | Line | Problem | 🔴🟡🟢 | Suggestion |`. Check: no behavior change · package manager unchanged · zero Nx Cloud traces · no versions in prose · hooks are native, committed, executable, and still block on failure · Nx `outputs` restore on warm runs · CI affected-based on MRs and full on default branch · build once, e2e reuses `dist/` · no secrets needed for build/test.

## Phase 5 — Verify & measure

- `<pm> run verify` = PASS, including every app-level unit and e2e script the repo defines (the full local gate, whatever it is named in this repo).
- Re-run Phase 0 measurements; report `| Metric | Before | After | Δ |` (cold and warm), including clean-install time, per-hook time, warm cache-hit rate, MR pipeline wall time.
- Revert any change without measurable gain or with flakiness. Then append an `## After` section to the run log that Phase 0 wrote (`docs/runs/<stamp>_chore-perf-optimize.md`): the `| Metric | Before | After | Δ |` table and the list of reverted plan items with the reason for each. Do not create a second run log and do not change the Phase 0 numbers.

## Done when

All approved plan items ✅ · review APPROVED · `<pm> run verify` PASS · before/after table delivered · CI pipeline green on an MR · package manager unchanged · Nx Cloud absent and guarded · hooks native · no version numbers in prose.
